{{Quote|Your melee weapon is made using a cortosis weave. It's strong enough to stand up against anything, even a lightsaber.|[[Trask Ulgo]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''</ref>}}
'''Cortosis''' [[Ore/Legends|ore]] was a very rare, brittle, fibrous material, the conductive properties of which would cause [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] to temporarily short out upon contact. This effect made cortosis a useful material for anti-lightsaber melee weapons, though with repeated strikes, a lightsaber could still cut through it. Cortosis, due to its energy resistant properties, was also resistant to blaster fire.

==Overview==
{{Quote|I never knew the proper name for the stuff. (...) I gather that if your lightsaber has dimetris circuits anywhere in the activation loop, hitting the rock starts a feedback crash running through the system that takes only a fraction of a second to shut the whole thing down.|[[Mara Jade Skywalker]] commenting on the cortosis ore's lightsaber-disabling property|<ref name="Vision of the Future">''[[Vision of the Future]]''</ref>}}
Cortosis [[Ore/Legends|ore]] was used extensively in [[shadowtrooper]] armor, as well as the [[C-B3 cortosis battle droid/Legends|C-B3 cortosis battle droids]] during the Clone Wars, and [[The Force/Legends|the Force]]-using group known as the [[Jensaarai/Legends|Jensaarai]]. The cortosis used for this armor was smuggled out from [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin's]] [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]]. The walls of the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Imperial Palace]] were also lined with cortosis ore. It was also used to strengthen starfighter and capital ship hulls, and was woven into body armor.

[[File:GiettKKruhk_JCAOW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|[[Micah Giiett]] educates [[K'Kruhk]] about cortosis.]]

Cortosis was expensive to mine because it was so rare and it had to be absolutely refined. Pure, unrefined, cortosis ore was for unexplained reasons, energized, [[Death/Legends|killing]] anyone who touched it with their bare skin, even [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]], who had energy-resistant enzymes in their sweat. Miners had to have filtering equipment, or else the cortosis particles would accumulate in their systems, causing hair loss, sickness, and eventually death. The substance was energy-resistant, meaning energy tools (such as plasma torches) were virtually useless. The brute force of hydraulic jacks were used to mine it, though it quickly wore the head of the jack to uselessness and its dust would clog the pistons. Pockets of highly-combustible [[lethane]] gas often formed near cortosis deposits.<ref name="Darth Plagueis novel">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>

The most valuable type of cortosis was the purified variation. It was known as ''Cortosis-Shield'', used by Roan Fel's Imperial Knights on their gauntlets. It was effective, even having more durability than [[Beskar/Legends|beskar]]. Demonstrating this Roan Fel cut a pauldron in two and could short out a lightsaber for a short period of time. Only [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsabers]] that used a special kind of [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|lightsaber crystal]] mined on [[Mestare]] were immune to the effects of cortosis.

==History==
During the [[New Sith Wars]], the [[Outer Rim Oreworks Company]] mined cortosis on [[Apatros/Legends|Apatros]]. This was where future [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth Bane/Legends|Darth Bane]] was born and drilled cortosis for several years before fleeing to the [[Fist of the Empire (group)|Sith Army]].

The [[Jin'ha]] mined cortosis on [[Obredaan]]. During the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], [[Trade Federation assassin droid]]s used cortosis weapons.<ref name="SW:OW">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>

During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]] discovered that the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] was mining cortosis on [[Bal'demnic/Legends|Bal'demnic]], and dispatched a task force led by [[Halagad Ventor]] and [[Sha Koon]] to [[Battle of Bal'demnic|sabotage the operation]].

[[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Micah Giiett]] owned a cortosis vambrace, and used it to educate padawans about lightsaber-resistant materials.

[[Anzat (species)|Anzati]] [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] [[Sajé Tasha]] wore a pair of clawed cortosis gauntlets during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].<ref name="Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Trackdown]]''</ref>

Large deposits of cortosis were also known to be on [[Duro/Legends|Duro]] and [[Katanos VII]].

[[Quinlan Vos/Legends|Quinlan Vos]] wore a [[Cortosis gauntlet/Legends|cortosis gauntlet]] on his left arm during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]

The [[Pau'an/Legends|Pau'an]] [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]], [[Darth Desolous]], used a [[Cortosis shield/Legends|cortosis shield]] to block lightsaber attacks.

[[Cad Bane/Legends|Cad Bane]] used a [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrower]] that fired [[cortosis shot]]s which he used against [[Bolla Ropal/Legends|Bolla Ropal]] to disable his lightsaber and capture him.

[[Galak Fyyar]] had an entire powered suit of shielded battle armor created out of cortosis alloy.

[[Riot stormtrooper/Legends|Riot stormtroopers]] were armed with [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaffs]] made with cortosis.

[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Mara Jade Skywalker|Mara Jade]] encountered a vein of cortosis on [[Nirauan/Legends|Nirauan]] while infiltrating the [[Hand of Thrawn]] during the [[Caamas Document Crisis]].

The [[Umbaran/Legends|Umbaran]] [[Nyss Nenn]] used twin [[Vibroblade/Legends|vibroblades]] coated with cortosis in combat. However, they proved ineffective against the [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitive]] [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] [[Soldier (clone)|Soldier]], who kept contact between their weapons minimal by striking fast, which therefore only caused his lightsaber to spark.

[[Roan Fel]] and all of his [[Imperial Knight]]s had pure [[Cortosis gauntlet/Legends|cortosis gauntlets]]. These gauntlets were worn by all of the [[Imperial Knight]]s who served [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Roan Fel]], and Fel, being a fully trained Knight himself, also wore a pair. The gauntlets act as protective shielding, the gauntlets were used by warriors who engaged in [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|lightsaber combat]]. [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] [[Darth Kruhl|Kruhl]] was surprised to find his weapon deactivate in the midst of [[Duel on Bastion|dueling]] Emperor Fel on [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]].<ref name="Legacy (2006) 13">[[Legacy (2006) 13|''Legacy'' (2006) 13]]</ref>

This bullet, upon striking a [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] blade, would cause the blade to short out, giving the shooter an advantage over the lightsaber wielder. ==Behind the scenes==
Sources conflict over the nature of cortosis and its effects on lightsabers. [[Old Republic era]] sources, such as the ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]'' video games, treated the effects of cortosis weapons as merely energy-resistant and only capable of blocking lightsaber attacks (though it may have been so due to gameplay mechanics, so cortosis blades wouldn't be too overpowered). This portrayal of cortosis is similar to that of [[Phrik/Legends|phrik]] and [[Beskar/Legends|Mandalorian iron]]. This is similar to the effect in [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']], where assassin droids which carry [[Cortosis sword/Legends|cortosis blades]] can block lightsabers but not shut them down. In the games ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', when the player slashes a shadowtrooper with their lightsaber, the saber will not be deactivated however the damage is reduced and slight "exploding" effects appear around the area the armor was struck. In ''[[Darth Bane: Path of Destruction]]'', a cortosis mine is described and cortosis is said to be incredibly dense and difficult to mine, but highly sought for its energy resistant properties that make it useful for weapons, armor, and in starship construction. In these sources, cortosis items and weapons are commonly used in the conflicts that make up the [[Dark Wars]] and the [[Sith civil war]]. This differs greatly from [[New Republic era|later-era]] portrayals, such as ''[[I, Jedi]]'', in which cortosis is described as a brittle, highly malleable metal capable not only of blocking energy attacks, but of disabling lightsaber weapons when it comes into contact with them.

Different types of cortosis have been named in various sources, such as cortosis alloy,<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref> purified cortosis,<ref name="Legacy 2006 13">[[Legacy (2006) 13|''Legacy'' (2006) 13]]</ref> and cortosis weave,<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic" /> but no consistent explanation for the different portrayals has been provided by sources.

The "shut-down" duration of time for the later-era portrayal of cortosis also varies in different sources. In ''[[Vision of the Future]]'', when Luke Skywalker first encounters it, it deactivates his lightsaber, but he is able to reignite the blade immediately. In other depictions, however, including [[Purge (comic book)|''Purge'']] and the [[Star Wars: Legacy|''Legacy'']] comic series, it renders lightsabers useless for several minutes.

===Cortosis Gauntlet===
According to [[Jan Duursema]], [[Darth Talon]] was able to cut off [[Elke Vetter]]'s hand despite her cortosis gauntlets because she cut at the point where the bracer and hand guard join, between the cortosis armor plates.<ref>{{DHBoards|url=viewtopic.php?t=16707#236057|thread=About the Imperial Knights' cortosis gaunltets|user=[[Jan Duursema|jan duursema]]|date=2010-01-02|time=10:42 pm}}</ref>
